task.title: Page one-shot schedule inventory through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/989 to expose bounded schedule inventory pages as deterministic read-only JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Validate page size and optional exact schedule-ID cursor before storage access.
Emit complete schedules and nullable next_after in deterministic exact-ID order.
Delegate selection and lookahead validation to read-only kernel storage and emit no partial stdout on failure.

attempts.diagnostic: The CLI rejected schedule page because the paging subcommand did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added focused CLI tests for ordering, continuation, terminal output, escaping, pre-storage validation, missing storage, and corruption isolation.

attempts.summary: Implemented and refactored the bounded adapter.
attempts.diagnostic: Implemented page-size and cursor validation, read-only list_page delegation, and compact continuation JSON using the complete schedule representation.
attempts.patch: Implemented issue 989 in crates/vela-dev/src/lib.rs with focused tests, ADR-0094, README usage, and scheduler documentation.

attempts.diagnostic: Independent review found no blocking issues; a rate-limited false green was excluded until genuine CodeRabbit run e1d12cf2 completed on exact head 03483e9 with no actionable comments and zero unresolved threads.
attempts.patch: Rechecked the shared review budget after cooldown, deliberately resumed review once, and armed merge only after exact-head CI and thread checks passed.

outcome.summary: Issue 989 delivered bounded schedule inventory JSON while preserving kernel paging and read-only authority.

verification.command: GitHub Rust quality gate for pull request 990 exact head 03483e9f8e1448ed8d4bcaf6603ee8f2e136de5c

lessons: CLI cursor validation must occur before storage access, while continuation truth remains kernel-owned.
Rate-limited CodeRabbit success is not review evidence; exact-head substantive review must complete before merge.
The adapter adds no clock, persisted cursor, status or due filtering, lifecycle, dispatch, permission, or execution authority.
